result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane roadway with minimal traffic calming and significant sidewalk obstructions. Parked vehicles frequently encroach upon the narrow, poorly maintained walkway, forcing pedestrians into the street or onto uneven surfaces.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are partially or fully blocking the narrow sidewalk on the right side of the image.

hazards.name: Wide Travel Lanes
hazards.description: The lack of clear lane markings and the overall width of the asphalt surface likely encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the narrow sidewalk and the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Widen the existing sidewalk to meet ADA standards and repair the degraded surface to ensure a continuous, accessible path.

interventions.title: Formalized On-Street Parking
interventions.description: Install curbs, bollards, or painted markings to clearly define parking areas and prevent vehicles from encroaching on the pedestrian walkway.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes and add marked parking or bike lanes to slow traffic and reduce crossing distances.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a narrow sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. Pedestrians are separated from traffic only by a curb and a line of parallel-parked vehicles, with utility poles further narrowing the effective walking width.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is situated within the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the clear path for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, on the sidewalk near the white car.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no planting strip or furniture zone separating the sidewalk from the parking lane and moving traffic, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible length of the sidewalk on the left.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk to provide a consistent clear path and introduce a furniture or planting zone to buffer pedestrians from the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: If this block leads to an intersection, curb extensions would shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The street is a wide, multi-lane residential thoroughfare with a central unpaved median and parallel parking. Pedestrian infrastructure is limited to narrow, obstructed sidewalks with no marked crossings or traffic calming measures visible.

hazards.name: Wide roadway and high speed potential
hazards.description: The excessive width of the travel lanes and the overall roadway encourages higher vehicle speeds in a residential context.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and parked vehicles on the left side of the image obstruct the clear walking path of the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge areas despite the residential land use and wide crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at regular intervals to provide designated crossing points.

interventions.title: Pedestrian refuge islands
interventions.description: Transform the existing median into a raised, protected refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide road in stages.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or mid-block to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses and wide sidewalks. While the environment is low-speed in nature, the near-side sidewalk is in poor condition with significant weed growth, and the continuous on-street parking creates potential visibility issues for pedestrians crossing mid-block.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Significant cracking and weed growth on the near-side sidewalk create tripping hazards and impede accessibility.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs of the roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repave the degraded sidewalk sections to provide a smooth, hazard-free walking surface and ensure ADA compliance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a marked mid-block crossing with appropriate signage to provide a designated and safer space for pedestrians to cross.
